mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 rally over the next 60 trading days as capital goods lag behind housing activity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes a decline in S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a statistically significant drop in returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered instances, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal income (PAYEMS) and a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) signals a divergence between income growth and spending, which historically precedes a decline in consumer discretionary equities and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 3-month average AND RSAFS < previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.4 percentage points in a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer demand and earnings pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which historically precedes muted S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a statistically significant decline in returns (p > 0.05).
